headline: School officials moved toward a major addition and renovation for Neary Elementary School after architects showed a base repair option leaves critical needs unfunded.
synopsis: Discussions this week centered on Margaret A. Neary Elementary School, where architects reported that a $15 million baseline repair budget yields only $5.8 million in direct construction due to state-mandated code upgrades, prompting the building committee to favor an estimated $38 million addition and renovation plan. At the same time, the School Committee learned that the ongoing Neary roof replacement is running significantly under budget with nearly $2 million expected to return to the town, and voted to align teacher salary schedules with Algonquin starting in 2027. Ahead of Special Town Meeting, the Golf Committee finalized its strategy to advocate for a major course irrigation funding article. The Board of Health approved a septic variance for a residential conversion, and the Tricentennial Committee executed a contract for a New Year's Day 2027 drone show.

highlights.title: Neary School $15 million base repair found insufficient
highlights.why: Architects demonstrated that a $15 million repair option nets only $5.8 million for construction after accounting for soft costs and code-mandated fire and accessibility upgrades, leaving boilers and HVAC systems unaddressed. The building committee prepared to advance schematic design for an estimated $38 million addition and renovation.

highlights.title: Neary roof replacement projected to return $2 million
highlights.why: School officials reported the Neary roof project is roughly 90 percent complete and significantly under budget. The district expects to return nearly $2 million of the original $4.5 million appropriation back to the town.

highlights.title: Teacher salary schedule aligned with Algonquin starting July 2027
highlights.why: The School Committee voted 5-0 to approve contract amendments with the Southborough Teachers Association Unit A. The agreement adjusts the retirement incentive program and aligns local teacher pay scales with Algonquin Regional High School beginning July 1, 2027.

highlights.title: Golf Committee plans outreach for Town Meeting irrigation article
highlights.why: The committee finalized its advocacy plan for a Special Town Meeting warrant article requesting roughly $350,000 in new Community Preservation Act funds and $100,000 from revolving funds. The article also seeks to extend the sunset date on $550,000 in previously authorized funds set to expire in December.

highlights.title: Tricentennial drone light show contract finalized for 2027
highlights.why: The committee executed a contract with Firefly for a 200-drone aerial light show to launch the town tricentennial on January 1, 2027. The show will launch from St. Mark's field and feature designs submitted by local middle school students.

highlights.title: Board of Health approves septic variance on Breakneck Hill Road
highlights.why: The board voted unanimously to grant an 85-foot wetland setback variance to convert a commercial property into a four-bedroom single-family home. The proposed system includes an advanced nitrogen-reduction treatment tank near a tributary to the Sudbury Reservoir.
